title: Day 76 · Week 10, Day 6 — Myths: bed rest protects a pregnancy, rest prevents preterm birth, and a woman who wasn't a runner shouldn't start moving now
summary: The Myths episode on rest. Bed rest became standard obstetric treatment on intuition, not trials. For bleeding in the first half of pregnancy, the only Cochrane evidence is two trials with 84 women and no benefit (RR 1.54, 0.92–2.58); ACOG says not to recommend it, because most early losses are chromosomal and set at conception, and exercise does not raise miscarriage risk (Davenport 2019, OR 0.88). For preterm birth, the one qualifying Cochrane trial (1,266 women) found no difference (RR 0.92); six twin trials (636 women) found no reduction in birth before 34 weeks; and in 646 women with a short cervix, the 39% placed on activity restriction delivered preterm in 37% vs 17% (aOR 2.37) — no benefit. The costs: one hospital series found blood clots in 15.6 per 1,000 women on bed rest vs 0.8 per 1,000 others; bone loss, muscle wasting, weight loss, depression and lost income. Then the beginner myth: ACOG, WHO and Canada say inactive women should start and build gradually; a 765-woman Madrid RCT starting at 9–11 weeks found non-exercisers had ~3× the odds of gestational hypertension. Where rest genuinely belongs (named contraindications, ordinary fatigue), the script for bleeding, and the one question to ask if bed rest is suggested.
action: Write one line at the top of the pregnancy file: 'Bleeding: call the practice the same day; bed rest is not the plan unless they give a specific reason,' with the after-hours number underneath. If your partner is just starting to move, book a 15-minute walk together for tomorrow.
